findings.pdf_says: A.4.3   Commit and Rollback  (printed as a third-level sub-clause of A.4, in the same bold heading style as 'A.4.1   General' and 'A.4.2   ACCEPT and DISPLAY screen handling' on page 974)
findings.why_it_matters: A.4.1 and A.4.2 are transcribed as '### A.4.1 General' / '### A.4.2 ACCEPT and DISPLAY screen handling' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 39849 and 39864), but A.4.3 is emitted at '##', the same level as its own parent '## A.4 Optional language element list' (line 39846). That makes the Commit-and-Rollback optional-element list a sibling of A.4 instead of a child, so any tool or reader that navigates by heading depth loses the containment relation and A.4's item list appears to end at A.4.2. The same demotion error affects A.4.4 through A.4.11 (lines 39948-40035) while A.4.12-A.4.14 (lines 40103-40115) are correctly at '###', so the file is internally inconsistent about the depth of one and the same clause level.
findings.suggested_repair: Change '## A.4.3 Commit and Rollback' to '### A.4.3 Commit and Rollback', and sweep the sibling headings A.4.4 through A.4.11 to '###' so all A.4.x clauses sit one level below '## A.4'.
